## The example groups

`judge_groups.txt` ships inside the package. Group A holds sentences
that are not literally true as written: a number “catches” payments,
silence “signs” an agreement, settings “load”. Group B holds sentences
that state a fact in the normal words for it, including instructions and
passives. The two groups cover a range of subjects and lengths. Some
group B sentences are unrelated to the rest, such as a greeting. We add
a sentence to group A when the check misses it in a real document, and
we add to group B or remove an example when the check flags a sentence
wrongly.

## Sentences

The model judges sentences, so
[`sentences`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/ai.html#sentences)
splits a document into them. It reads the paragraphs and list items that
[`segment`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/segment.html#segment)
returns. Headings are left out, and
[`segment`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/segment.html#segment)
has already dropped fenced code, tables and block quotes. spaCy finds
the sentence boundaries in each line of the scrubbed text, where inline
code cannot confuse it. Each
[`Sent`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/ai.html#sent) holds
the sentence on one line as a reader sees it. Inline code stays. Link
targets and emphasis markers are removed, since scrubbing turned them
into spaces. It also keeps its offsets in the document and the index of
its paragraph.

Fragments of fewer than `min_words` words are skipped. Most are list
items such as “fast startup”, which have no verb to judge.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/ai.py#L60"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>


*Sentences of `min_words`+ words in the paragraphs and list items of
markdown `txt`; a newline ends a sentence*

### Sent

``` python
def Sent(
    start, # Character offset of the sentence in the document
    end, # Character offset one past its end
    text, # The sentence on one line, with inline code kept and other markup removed
    para, # Index of its paragraph or list item among the judged blocks
):
```

This document has a heading, a wrapped paragraph with inline code, a
fenced block, and a list:

```` python
DOC = """# widget

Rows carry their source. Call `enhance()` to start.
fork    exact clone of this session

```python
rows.carry(source)  # code is never judged
```

- [Each event](events.md) knows its *timestamp*.
- fast startup
"""
ss = sentences(DOC)
ss
````

The offsets locate each sentence in the document. A newline always ends
a sentence. The third line of `DOC` has no full stop and is one
sentence. The list marker is not part of the text:

``` python
test_eq([s.text for s in ss], ['Rows carry their source.', 'Call `enhance()` to start.', 'fork exact clone of this session', 'Each event knows its timestamp.'])
test_eq(DOC[ss[2].start:ss[2].end], 'fork    exact clone of this session')
test_eq([s.para for s in ss], [0, 0, 0, 1])
```

Some prompt files wrap their sections in tags such as `<rules>`.
[`sentences`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/ai.html#sentences)
drops a tag that has a line to itself, and keeps other text in angle
brackets, such as a placeholder. It also rejoins a sentence that spaCy
splits in the wrong place. One such place is a full stop with no space
after it, as in `Answer.AI`. Another is a place with no full stop at
all, such as before “so” in the second sentence here:

``` python
tagged = "<rules>\nWe work without an Answer.AI account. Asset URLs carry a content hash (`vsrc`) so browsers can cache them.\nCheck each notebook with nbdev-test <nb>\n</rules>\n"
test_eq([s.text for s in sentences(tagged)], ['We work without an Answer.AI account.', 'Asset URLs carry a content hash (`vsrc`) so browsers can cache them.',
    'Check each notebook with nbdev-test <nb>'])
```

spaCy also splits some sentences that are whole.
[`sentences`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/ai.html#sentences)
rejoins three kinds. A colon does not end a sentence, so a label stays
with what it introduces. A passage in double quotes stays in one piece,
even when it holds a full stop. A full stop after a common abbreviation,
such as “incl.” or “cf.”, does not end a sentence when the next word
does not start with a capital letter:

``` python
dense = """- run: glyphs, names, groups, no spaces between. runs: `+/÷≢`, `x.[1 2]`.
- Open with "NB: this file is for an LLM reader, not a human. Add it to your context." It tells a person why the file reads oddly.
- status: ask it to report, incl. long runs. MUST NOT brief it.
"""
test_eq([s.text for s in sentences(dense)], ['run: glyphs, names, groups, no spaces between.', 'runs: `+/÷≢`, `x.[1 2]`.',
    'Open with "NB: this file is for an LLM reader, not a human. Add it to your context."', 'It tells a person why the file reads oddly.',
    'status: ask it to report, incl. long runs.', 'MUST NOT brief it.'])
```

[`scrub`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/segment.html#scrub)
blanks some text that a reader sees, as if it were markup: a bare URL or
autolink, and a name such as `__call__`, whose underscores look like
emphasis.
[`sentences`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/ai.html#sentences)
copies these back from the source before it splits, so a sentence keeps
them:

``` python
seen = "Docs: https://fastcore.fast.ai/tools.html.md and https://fastcore.fast.ai/nbio.html.md\nCall the op object, never type(op).__call__ directly.\n"
test_eq([s.text for s in sentences(seen)], ['Docs: https://fastcore.fast.ai/tools.html.md and https://fastcore.fast.ai/nbio.html.md',
    'Call the op object, never type(op).__call__ directly.'])
```

A long document goes to the model in chunks of about 1,000 words, the
size the prompt was tested on.
[`_chunks`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/ai.html#_chunks)
never divides a paragraph. Sentence numbers run through the whole
document.

``` python
cs = _chunks(ss, max_words=10)
test_eq([[i for i,_ in c] for c in cs], [[0, 1, 2], [3]])
```

## The prompt

[`ai_prompt`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/ai.html#ai_prompt)
gives the model one sentence of framing, the two groups, and the
numbered sentences with a blank line between paragraphs. With a `seed`
it shuffles the order of the examples in each group. It asks for a
verdict on every line. A list of only the flagged numbers would be
shorter, but in tests it found fewer of the sentences we wanted.

`SYSTEM` stops `gemini-3.8-flash` from thinking before it answers.
Without it the model thinks in most calls, which costs several times
more and finds no more.

## Results

An
[`AIFinding`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/ai.html#aifinding)
is one sentence that at least one run flagged. Its weight is the number
of runs that flagged it. An
[`AIResult`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/ai.html#airesult)
keeps every sentence sent to the model in `sents`. `votes` holds the
number of runs that flagged each one, and `judged` the number that gave
any verdict on it. A failed call or an incomplete reply lowers `judged`.
`missing` is the total of verdicts that never came back. The report
shows it when it is above zero. The density is the percentage of the
sentences flagged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/slopometer/blob/main/slopometer/ai.py#L168"

Two of five runs flagged the first sentence here. One run gave no
verdict on the last:

``` python
r = AIResult(DOC, scored_words(segment(DOC)), ss, [2, 0, 0, 0], [5, 5, 5, 4])
test_eq((len(r.findings), r.density, r.worst, r.missing), (1, 25.0, 2, 1))
test_eq(r.as_dict()['sentences'][3]['line'], 10)
r
```

## Judging texts and files

Each call returns the verdicts for one chunk, or the exception if the
call failed.
[`_count`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/ai.html#_count) adds
them up for each sentence, reading only the chunk’s own sentence numbers
from a reply.

Here three runs judge one chunk of two sentences. The first reply covers
both, the second leaves one out, and the third call fails:

``` python
jobs = [(0, list(enumerate(ss[:2])), run) for run in range(3)]
outs = [{0: True, 1: False}, {0: True}, TimeoutError()]
test_eq(_count(jobs, outs, [2]), ([[2, 0]], [[2, 1]]))
```

[`ai_texts`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/ai.html#ai_texts)
judges several documents at once. Every chunk of every document is sent
`runs` times, and all of those calls share one limit of `n_workers` at a
time. Each run shuffles the examples with its run number as the seed.
With thinking off, runs of one identical prompt give nearly identical
answers, and repeating them finds nothing new. A sentence is flagged
when any run flags it. A document with no sentence to judge gets no
request.

A call that fails does not stop the others. Each result reports how many
verdicts are missing.
[`ai_texts`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/ai.html#ai_texts)
raises an error only when no verdict came back at all, since that run
says nothing about any document.

### ai_texts

``` python
async def ai_texts(
    txts, # Markdown documents
    runs:int=5, # Times to send each chunk
    model:str='gemini/models/gemini-3.8-flash', # `fastllm` model path
    n_workers:int=16, # Model calls in flight at once, across all documents
):
```

*One
[`AIResult`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/slopometer/ai.html#airesult)
per document in `txts`, flagging each sentence that any run calls hard*

A document with no sentence to judge gets no request and no findings:

``` python
empty = (await ai_texts(['# Only a heading\n\n- fast startup\n']))[0]
test_eq((empty.sents, empty.findings, empty.density), ([], [], 0.0))
```

With `GEMINI_API_KEY` set, judge a file or a directory. `--ai` on the
command line does the same:

``` python
rs = await ai_paths('08_corpus.ipynb')
rs[0]
```
